Source: Atlas do Desenvolvimento Humano no Brasil (PNUD, Ipea, FJP),
site Acervo > Bases de dados, card "Censo Demográfico (1991, 2000 e
2010)", file `censo_total_1991_2010.xlsx`, downloaded 2026-10-13
(`_data/raw/atlas/`). Indicator set of the 2013 Atlas edition on the
three census vintages. Dictionary in the sheet `Siglas`.
Consumer: the descriptive sprint script `_scripts/09-descriptive-data.R`
(tasks 4.2, 4.3); promoted to the pipeline under task 4.8.
The lost legacy input was a Consulta export without geocodes, matched on
municipality names with an alias table (`07-data-analysis-EDA-poverty.R`,
parked in `_annex/parked/` since phase 2R, 2026-10-30).
This file carries the seven-digit IBGE code, so the join is exact.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
f <- "_data/raw/atlas/censo_total_1991_2010.xlsx"
siglas <- read_excel(f, sheet = "Siglas")
mun <- read_excel(f, sheet = "MUN 91-00-10") %>%
  mutate(geocode = as.integer(Codmun7), year = as.integer(ANO))
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation) %>%
  mutate(geocode = as.integer(geocode))
biome <- read_delim("_data/raw/ibge/ibge_bioma.csv", delim = ";",
                    show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  rename(geocode = 1, nome = 2, uf = 3, bioma = 4) %>%
  mutate(geocode = as.integer(geocode)) %>%
  filter(str_detect(bioma, "Amaz"))
```

## Q1. What is the layout and the release of the workbook?

```{r q1-layout}
excel_sheets(f)
tibble(sheet = c("Siglas", "MUN 91-00-10"), rows = c(nrow(siglas), nrow(mun)),
       cols = c(ncol(siglas), ncol(mun)))
mun %>% count(year)
siglas %>% filter(SIGLA %in% c("PIND", "PMPOB", "PPOB", "GINI", "RDPC", "IDHM",
                               "pesourb", "pesoRUR", "pesotot", "POP")) %>%
  select(SIGLA, `NOME CURTO`, `DEFINIÇÃO`) %>% mutate(`DEFINIÇÃO` = str_trunc(`DEFINIÇÃO`, 110))
```

**Finding.** One municipal sheet, 5,565 municipalities in each of 1991,
2000 and 2010, 237 columns, identified by `Codmun7`; a 237-row dictionary
travels with the file. The indicators the chapter needs are present:
`PIND`, `PMPOB`, `PPOB` (extreme poverty, poverty, vulnerability),
`GINI`, `RDPC`, `IDHM`, and the urban and rural population counts
`pesourb` and `pesoRUR`.
**Decision.** none required; provenance row written 2026-10-13.

## Q2. Do all three vintages join completely on geocode?

```{r q2-join}
join <- mun %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>% count(year, name = "sample_rows")
join
missing_sample <- setdiff(sample_geo$geocode, mun$geocode)
missing_biome <- setdiff(biome$geocode, mun$geocode)
dup <- mun %>% count(geocode, year) %>% filter(n > 1)
tibble(sample_missing = length(missing_sample), biome_list_missing = length(missing_biome),
       duplicate_keys = nrow(dup))
biome %>% filter(geocode %in% missing_biome) %>% select(geocode, nome, uf)
```

**Finding.** Every one of the 502 sample municipalities is present in the
three vintages, with no duplicate geocode-year key. The one absentee,
from the 503-municipality MapBiomas extract and from the biome list
alike, is Mojuí dos Campos (installed 2013, after the last census;
dropped from the sample in script 05, D-2026-10-05-l), so the Atlas
carries nothing for it in any vintage, which is consistent with its
parent rule in task 1.6.
**Decision.** none required; join on `Codmun7`, the legacy name match
and its alias table are retired.
**Assertion.** `09-descriptive-data.R`, Atlas block: 502 x 3 rows after
the join.

## Q3. Do the names agree with the panel, as a check on the code join?

```{r q3-names}
norm <- function(x) x %>% str_to_lower() %>% stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") %>%
  str_replace_all("[^a-z ]", "") %>% str_squish()
names_chk <- mun %>% filter(year == 2010, geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  select(geocode, atlas_name = `Município`) %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  filter(norm(atlas_name) != norm(municipality))
nrow(names_chk)
names_chk %>% select(geocode, atlas_name, municipality, state_abbreviation)
```

**Finding.** Two names differ, both spelling variants of the same place
(Eldorado dos/do Carajás, Santa Isabel/Izabel do Pará), the kind of case
the legacy alias table had to patch by hand. Neither signals a wrong
code.
**Decision.** none required.

## Q4. Are the poverty shares on a 0-100 scale and nested?

```{r q4-scale}
pov <- mun %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  select(year, PIND, PMPOB, PPOB, GINI)
pov %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(c(PIND, PMPOB, PPOB, GINI),
                   list(min = min, median = median, max = max), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-year) %>% separate(name, c("var", "stat"), sep = "_(?=[a-z]+$)") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
pov %>% summarise(nested = all(PIND <= PMPOB & PMPOB <= PPOB), any_na = any(is.na(PMPOB)))
```

**Finding.** The three shares run from 0 to 100 and nest as the
definitions require (extreme poverty within poverty within vulnerability)
in every sample row; the Gini sits on 0-1. The sample median of the
poverty share falls from 68 percent in 1991 to 57 in 2000 and 40 in
2010, with the extreme-poverty median from 37 to 21.
**Decision.** open: script 09 stores the shares divided by 100, so the
Atlas columns sit on the same 0-1 scale as the panel's other shares
(naming per the convention grammar); logged as a D-ID when the script
lands.

## Q5. Do the urban and rural counts add up, and is the urban share plausible?

```{r q5-urban}
urb <- mun %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  mutate(sum_ok = abs(pesourb + pesoRUR - pesotot) <= 1,
         urban_share = pesourb / pesotot)
urb %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(sum_ok = mean(sum_ok), pop_vs_pesotot = median(POP / pesotot),
            urban_min = min(urban_share), urban_q1 = quantile(urban_share, .25),
            urban_median = median(urban_share), urban_q3 = quantile(urban_share, .75),
            urban_max = max(urban_share), .groups = "drop")
urb %>% filter(year == 2010) %>% left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  count(state_abbreviation, rural_majority = urban_share < 0.5) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = rural_majority, values_from = n, values_fill = 0,
              names_prefix = "rural_majority_")
```

**Finding.** Urban plus rural equals the total population in every row.
`POP` (population in permanent private households) runs about one
percent below `pesotot`, as expected. The sample's median urban share
rises from 0.34 in 1991 to 0.53 in 2010, and in 2010 some 215 of the 502
municipalities (43 percent) still have a rural majority, most of them in
Pará, Maranhão and Amazonas, which gives task 4.2 a real split to work
with.
**Decision.** open: `pesourb / pesotot` is the urban share for task 4.2;
`pesotot` is the Atlas population, not a substitute for the census
anchors already in the panel.

## Q6. What is the price base of the income variable?

```{r q6-income}
cat(strwrap(siglas$`DEFINIÇÃO`[siglas$SIGLA == "RDPC"], 90), sep = "\n")
cat(strwrap(siglas$`DEFINIÇÃO`[siglas$SIGLA == "PMPOB"], 90), sep = "\n")
mun %>% filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(rdpc_median = median(RDPC), rdpc_max = max(RDPC), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** The dictionary states the base: reais of 1 August 2010 for
the income per capita, and the poverty lines (R$ 140 a month for
poverty) are expressed in the same reais, so the three vintages are
directly comparable.
**Decision.** open: script 09 deflates `RDPC` to 2024 reais with the
panel's IPCA deflator (`_data/aux/deflator_ipca_2024.csv`) from the 2010
base, so the Atlas income sits beside `gdp_per_capita_2024`; the exact
monthly anchor is checked against the deflator table when the script
lands.
